spots.name: Cathedral of Learning

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral of Learning is a 42-story skyscraper that serves as the centerpiece of the University of Pittsburgh's (Pitt) main campus in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

spots.name: Fort Duquesne
spots.summary: Fort Duquesne was a fort established by the French in 1754, at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers. It was later taken over by the British, and later the Americans, and developed as Pittsburgh in Pennsylvania.

spots.name: PPG Place
spots.summary: PPG Place is a complex in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, consisting of six buildings within three city blocks and five and a half acres. PPG Place was designed by architects Philip Johnson and John Burgee.

spots.name: Carnegie Museum of Natural History

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Carnegie Museum of Natural History is a natural history museum in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It was founded by Pittsburgh-based industrialist Andrew Carnegie in 1896. Housing some 22 million specimens, the museum features extensive paleontological and entomological collections.

spots.name: BNY Mellon Center

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: BNY Mellon Center is a 55-story skyscraper located at 500 Grant Street in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Standing 725 ft (221 m) tall, it is the second-tallest building in the city. Announced on March 27, 1980, the tower was completed in June 1984.

spots.name: The Andy Warhol Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Andy Warhol Museum is located on the North Shore of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. It is the largest museum in North America dedicated to a single artist. The museum holds an extensive permanent collection of art and archives from the Pittsburgh-born pop art icon Andy Warhol.

spots.name: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
spots.summary: Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens is a botanical garden set in Schenley Park in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. It is a City of Pittsburgh historic landmark and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

spots.name: USS Requin

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: USS Requin, a Tench-class submarine, was the only ship of the United States Navy to be named after the requin, French for shark. Since 1990 she has been a museum ship at the Kamin Science Center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

spots.name: Roberto Clemente Bridge
spots.summary: The Roberto Clemente Bridge, also known as the Sixth Street Bridge, spans the Allegheny River in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States.

photo.author: David Trainer from Mosteiros, Cape Verde

spots.name: Duquesne Incline
spots.summary: The Duquesne Incline is a funicular scaling Mount Washington near the South Side neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States.

spots.name: Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh is a nonprofit organization that operates four museums in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. The organization is headquartered in the Carnegie Institute and Library complex in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh.

spots.name: Carnegie Museum of Art
spots.summary: The Carnegie Museum of Art is an art museum in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. The museum was originally known as the Department of Fine Arts, Carnegie Institute and was located at what became the Main Branch of the Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh.

spots.name: Fort Pitt
spots.summary: Fort Pitt was a fort built by British forces between 1759 and 1761 during the French and Indian War at the confluence of the Monongahela and Allegheny rivers, where the Ohio River is formed in western Pennsylvania.

photo.author: Downtown_Pittsburgh_May_2008.jpg: Allie Caufield derivative work: GrapedApe (tal

spots.name: Allegheny Cemetery
spots.summary: Allegheny Cemetery is one of the largest and oldest burial grounds in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is a historic rural cemetery.

spots.name: Heinz Memorial Chapel

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Heinz Memorial Chapel is a Pittsburgh History and Landmarks Foundation Historic Landmark and a contributing property to the Schenley Farms National Historic District on the campus of the University of Pittsburgh in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States.

photo.author: Ryan Kelly from New York/Atlanta, USA

spots.name: National Aviary
spots.summary: The National Aviary, located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, is the only independent indoor nonprofit aviary in the United States. The facility is also the country's largest indoor aviary, and the only one accorded honorary "National" status by the United States Congress.

spots.name: Fort Pitt Bridge
spots.summary: The Fort Pitt Bridge is a steel, double-decked bowstring arch bridge that spans the Monongahela River near its confluence with the Allegheny River in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It carries Interstate 376 between the Fort Pitt Tunnel and Downtown Pittsburgh.

photo.author: The original uploader was Cacophony at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Gulf Tower
spots.summary: The Gulf Tower is a 44-story, 177.4 m (582 ft) Art Deco skyscraper in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The tower is one of the major distinctive and recognizable features of the city and is named for the Gulf Oil Corporation.

spots.name: St. Paul Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Saint Paul Cathedral is the mother church of the Diocese of Pittsburgh in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, in the United States.

spots.name: Allegheny County Courthouse
spots.summary: The Allegheny County Courthouse in Downtown Pittsburgh, is part of a complex designed by H. H. Richardson. The buildings are considered among the finest examples of the Romanesque Revival style for which Richardson is well known.

spots.name: Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall and Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall and Museum is a National Register of Historic Places landmark that is located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. It is the largest memorial in the United States that is dedicated solely to honoring all branches of military veterans and service personnel.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Soldiers and Sailors Memorial Hall and Museum

photo.author: The original uploader was Willjay at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Kamin Science Center
spots.summary: The Kamin Science Center, formerly known as the Carnegie Science Center, is one of the four Carnegie Museums of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is located in the Chateau neighborhood, across the street from Acrisure Stadium.

spots.name: Fifth Avenue Place

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Fifth Avenue Place is a skyscraper in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. The building is owned by Highmark subsidiary Jenkins Empire Associates and has served as the company's headquarters since it was completed in 1988.

spots.name: Koppers Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Koppers Building is a historical building in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, commissioned by Andrew W. Mellon and completed in 1929. The building is named after the Koppers Chemical Corporation and is one of the major features of Downtown Pittsburgh.

spots.name: Monongahela Incline
spots.summary: The Monongahela Incline is a funicular on the South Side of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States, near the Smithfield Street Bridge. Designed and built by Prussian-born engineer John Endres in 1870, it is the oldest continuously operating funicular in the United States.

spots.name: Fort Duquesne Bridge
spots.summary: The Fort Duquesne Bridge is a steel bowstring arch bridge that spans the Allegheny River in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It was colloquially referred to as "The Bridge to Nowhere" prior to its completion.

spots.name: Canton Avenue
spots.summary: Canton Avenue is a street in Pittsburgh's Beechview neighborhood which is the steepest officially recorded public street in the United States.

spots.name: Regional Enterprise Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Alcoa Building is a 410-foot-tall (120 m) skyscraper in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It was completed in 1953 and has 31 floors. It is the 15th-tallest building in the city and is adjacent to Mellon Square.

spots.name: Pittsburgh Athletic Association
spots.summary: The Pittsburgh Athletic Association at the University of Pittsburgh is a historic, Benno Janssen designed building located in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Opened as the home of a private social and athletic club of the same name, the building is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

spots.name: Point State Park
spots.summary: Point State Park is a Pennsylvania state park which is located on 36 acres (150,000 m2) in Downtown Pittsburgh, Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, U.S., at the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers, forming the Ohio River.

spots.name: Schenley Farms Historic District
spots.summary: The Schenley Farms Historic District, also referred to as the Schenley Farms–Oakland Civic District, is a historic district listed on the National Register of Historic Places that is located in the Oakland section of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States.

spots.name: Allegheny County Jail
spots.summary: The Allegheny County Jail is the municipal jail of Allegheny County, located at 950 Second Avenue in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The current facility, completed in 1995, replaced the old jail, which is attached to the Allegheny County Courthouse and now serves court functions.

spots.name: Andy Warhol Bridge
spots.summary: Andy Warhol Bridge, also known as the Seventh Street Bridge, spans the Allegheny River in Downtown Pittsburgh. It is the only bridge in the United States named for a visual artist. It was opened as the Seventh Street Bridge at a cost of $1.5 million on June 17, 1926, in a ceremony attended by 2,000 people.

spots.name: Smithfield Street Bridge
spots.summary: The Smithfield Street Bridge is a lenticular truss bridge crossing the Monongahela River in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. The bridge was designed by Gustav Lindenthal, the engineer who later designed the Hell Gate Bridge in New York City.

spots.name: First Presbyterian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The First Presbyterian Church of Pittsburgh is an active congregation in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA. The church structure in use today was completed in 1905.

spots.name: Stephen Foster Memorial

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The Stephen Collins Foster Memorial is a performing arts center and museum which houses the Stephen Foster Archives at the University of Pittsburgh in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA. It is dedicated to the life and works of American songwriter Stephen Foster.

spots.name: Rachel Carson Bridge
spots.summary: The Rachel Carson Bridge, also known as the Ninth Street Bridge, spans the Allegheny River in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania in the United States.

spots.name: Oliver Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Henry W. Oliver Building, now known as the Embassy Suites By Hilton Pittsburgh Downtown, is a 25-story, 106 m (348 ft) skyscraper at 535 Smithfield Street, across from Mellon Square in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

spots.name: One PPG Place

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: PPG Place is a complex in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, consisting of six buildings within three city blocks and five and a half acres. PPG Place was designed by architects Philip Johnson and John Burgee.

spots.name: Acrisure Stadium
spots.summary: Acrisure Stadium, formerly known as Heinz Field, is a stadium located in the North Shore neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, U.S. It primarily serves as the home of the Pittsburgh Steelers of the National Football League (NFL) and the Pittsburgh Panthers of the National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA).

spots.name: One PNC Plaza

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: One PNC Plaza is a high-rise office building located in the Golden Triangle neighborhood of the Central Business District of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. Constructed in 1972, it is 129.24 m (424.0 ft) 30 stories. It houses the general offices for PNC Financial Services.

spots.name: Grant Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Grant Building is 40-story, 147.8 m (485 ft) skyscraper at 310 Grant Street in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The building was completed and opened on February 1, 1929 at a cost of $5.5 million. The Art Deco building's facade is built with Belgian granite, limestone, and brick.

photo.author: View_of_Pittsburgh.jpg: Allie Caufield derivative work: GrapedApe (talk)

spots.name: Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Carnegie Library of Pittsburgh is the public library system in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Its main branch is located in the Oakland neighborhood of Pittsburgh, and it has 19 branch locations throughout the city.

spots.name: Gateway Center
spots.summary: Gateway Center is a complex of office, residential, and hotel buildings covering 25 acres (10 ha) in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It lies between Commonwealth Place and Stanwix Street at the western edge of the central business district, immediately to the east of Point State Park.

photo.author: Downtown_Pittsburgh_May_2005.jpg: Allie Caufield derivative work: GrapedApe (tal

spots.name: William S. Moorhead Federal Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The William S. Moorhead Federal Building is a 340-foot (100 m)-tall skyscraper that is located in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. Plans for the building were announced on November 9, 1958, and the structure was completed in 1964.

spots.name: PNC Park
spots.summary: PNC Park is a baseball stadium on the North Shore of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is the fifth location to serve as the home ballpark of Major League Baseball's Pittsburgh Pirates. Opened during the 2001 MLB season, PNC Park sits along the Allegheny River with a view of the Downtown Pittsburgh skyline.

spots.name: David McCullough Bridge
spots.summary: The David McCullough Bridge, commonly and historically known as the 16th Street Bridge, is a steel trussed through arch bridge that spans the Allegheny River in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

spots.name: Grant Street
spots.summary: Grant Street is the main government and business corridor in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It is home to the global headquarters of U.S. Steel, Koppers Chemicals, and Oxford Development. It also is home to the seat of Allegheny County, City of Pittsburgh and the regional Federal Government offices.

spots.name: Wabash Bridge
spots.summary: The Wabash Bridge was a railroad bridge across the Monongahela River at Pittsburgh. It was constructed between 1902 and 1904 by railroad magnate George J. Gould for his Wabash Pittsburgh Terminal Railway.

spots.name: Trinity Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Trinity Cathedral is an Episcopal Church in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and is the cathedral for the Episcopal Diocese of Pittsburgh.

spots.name: Mellon Square
spots.summary: Mellon Square is an urban park in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States. It is the first Modernist park built above a parking garage. With its distinctive black, white, and green geometric pavement, it is a prominent urban oasis and gathering spot in Downtown Pittsburgh.

spots.name: Pittsburgh City-County Building
spots.summary: The Pittsburgh City-County Building is the seat of government for the City of Pittsburgh, and houses both city and Allegheny County offices. It is located in Downtown Pittsburgh at 414 Grant Street. Built from 1915 to 1917 it is the third seat of government of Pittsburgh.

spots.name: Duquesne Club
spots.summary: The Duquesne Club is a private social club in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Since its founding in 1873, it has functioned as one of the most exclusive social clubs in the world, and as a meeting place for businessmen, civic leaders, politicians, and royalty around the world.

spots.name: Market Square
spots.summary: Market Square is a public space located in Downtown Pittsburgh at the intersection of Forbes Avenue and Market Street. The square was home to the first courthouse and first jail, and the first newspaper west of the Allegheny Mountains, the Pittsburgh Gazette (1786).

spots.name: Point Bridge
spots.summary: The Point Bridge was a steel cantilever truss bridge that spanned the Monongahela River in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

photo.author: David Wilson from Oak Park, Illinois, USA

spots.name: Federated Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Federated Hermes Tower is a 358-foot-tall (109 m) skyscraper in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The building is part of Liberty Center, a two-building complex which also includes the Westin Convention Center Hotel. It was completed in 1986 and has 27 floors and 530,000 square feet (49,000 m2) of space.

spots.name: Schenley Plaza
spots.summary: Schenley Plaza is a public park serving as the grand entrance into Schenley Park in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

spots.name: St. Stanislaus Kostka Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Stanislaus Kostka Church in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, referred to in Polish as Kościół Świętego Stanisława Kostki, is a historic church of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Pittsburgh.

spots.name: South Tenth Street Bridge
spots.summary: The South Tenth Street Bridge, most often called the Tenth Street Bridge, but officially dubbed the Philip Murray Bridge, is a suspension bridge that spans the Monongahela River in Downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

spots.name: Church of the Epiphany

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Church of the Epiphany is a church located at Washington Place and Centre Avenue in the Hill District neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, was built in 1902. The church was added to the List of Pittsburgh History and Landmarks Foundation Historic Landmarks in 1998. It is situated next to PPG Paints Arena.

spots.name: Frick Building
spots.summary: A 20-story building constructed by the industrialist Henry Clay Frick in 1902. The building sports many lavish features, such as marble ceilings, intricate grillwork, and stained glass windows.

spots.name: Union Trust Building
spots.summary: A gorgeous Flemish-Gothic structure built in 1916 by Henry Clay Frick, the structure is decorated with a steep mansard roof, terra cotta dormers, and two chapel-like towers. The church-like appearance of the structure owes to the previous use of the land, a nineteenth century catholic cathedral.

spots.name: William Pitt Union
spots.summary: Built as the Schenley Hotel in 1898, this historic beaux-arts building that was Pittsburgh's premier luxury hotel in its day. As a hotel, it hosted many dignitaries including four Presidents of the United States, a slew of Hollywood celebrities such as Lillian Russell and Katharine Hepburn, along with many of the visiting baseball teams that played across the street at Forbes Field. The turn-of-th

photo.author: The original uploader was Crazypaco at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: U.S. Steel Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A 64-story triangular office building which is the tallest in Pittsburgh, and briefly held the honor of being the tallest building in the world outside of New York City and Chicago. It was built in 1971 of a special type of steel, "Corten" steel, developed by USS. It is not painted and is intended to rust to a tough, brown finish and then stop rusting. (One hopes.)

spots.name: Alumni Hall
spots.summary: Freely accessible to the public, Alumni Hall is a restored former Masonic Greek Revival temple completed by Benno Janssen in 1915. The facility contains many of its original elements, the University's [http://www.legacy.pitt.edu/ Legacy Gallery] of electronic kiosks in its lobby, a gallery of portraits of the university chancellors stretching back 200 years on the Connolly Ballroom's balcony, and

spots.name: First Lutheran Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This lovely church looks particularly out of place next to the massive office buildings surrounding it, but serves as an interesting reminder that this was once a residential area.

spots.name: One Oxford Centre
spots.summary: A gleaming white set of buildings, the tallest of which is the city's fifth tallest. At night they are lit up rather nicely.

spots.name: Frick Fine Arts Building
spots.summary: Designed to reflect an Italian Renaissance villa, this building contains in its cloister a large collection of scale reproductions by Russian artist Nicholas Lochoff of 15th-century Italian Renaissance masterpieces, considered to be among the best copies in the world. The building is open to public and free to explore. It is also home to the [https://uag.pitt.edu/ University Art Gallery], which co

spots.name: David L. Lawrence Convention Center
spots.summary: The convention center is quite a sight, with its sweeping design facing the Allegheny River. Be sure to walk up to the entrance on 10th Street near Penn Avenue - a walkway starts there that runs underneath the building towards the shore of the Allegheny River. The walkway is flanked on both sides by illuminated waterfalls.

spots.name: Miller Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A very nice and often intriguing contemporary art gallery with constantly changing exhibits.

spots.name: Station Square
spots.summary: Now a popular office and shopping complex, Station Square used to be a railroad station. The station, fully renovated, is still there. Now housing the Gandy Dancer Saloon and the Grand Concourse restaurant, it is a beautiful example of the grand train stations of the past with a huge, beautiful colored glass skylight, feaux marble columns and fine wooden appointments. You may still see a train pas

spots.name: Senator John Heinz History Center
spots.summary: An affiliate of the Smithsonian Institution and the largest history museum in Pennsylvania. Featuring 6 floors of permanent and changing exhibitions, this museum gives a very detailed look at the past 250 years in Western Pennsylvania, with displays on Pittsburgh-area innovations, people, and industries. Notable exhibits include artifacts from the French & Indian War, a hall dedicated to the Heinz

spots.name: Hemingways

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: $1 Miller Lites, microbrew selection, combined with the food, great place to drink. A lot of girls. Usually so packed during the school year it's hard to order a drink...or even move. As with many places in the U.S. don't be fooled by the $1 draft drink specials as you're getting a small plastic cup of beer, not a pint. Pay attention to happy hour specials. Half of food (on a special menu) 11AM-11

spots.name: Primanti Brothers

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Founded in 1934 to serve the truckers that brought vegetables to the Strip, Primanti is famous for their sandwiches. There are various locations around town, but the one in the Strip is the original, open 24 hours. If you are in Pittsburgh, you need to eat here at least once; they serve sandwiches with the french fries and coleslaw right in the sandwich with whatever else you order: deli meat, hot

spots.name: Pamela's Diner
spots.summary: This local chain has been in Oakland for years. It is the place to go in the neighborhood for breakfast. They are famous for, well, many things, but particularly their crepe hotcakes, decadent waffles and pancakes, and omelets. Barack Obama was so impressed during a campaign stop in Pittsburgh, he had Pamela's cater at the Whitehouse. Be aware that the wait on weekends can get very long.

spots.name: Enrico Biscotti Cafe
spots.summary: This rustic cafe serves fresh pizzas made in their own wood-burning brick oven. Besides fresh pizza they serve beans and greens, home made soups, and big fat salads. Stop at the bakery for great biscotti, made by hand and served in an abundance of flavors. The bakery serves all sorts of Italian pastries so even if biscotti's not your cup of tea, you will be able to enjoy the place.

spots.name: Primanti Bros.

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Sun

spots.summary: A local chain, Primantis offers the quintessential Pittsburgh sandwich. No trip to Pittsburgh is complete without experiencing one of their coleslaw and french fry topped extravaganzas. Profiled in numerous national programs and articles, if you only have time to eat at a Primantis once during your trip to Pittsburgh, than Oakland has this location ready for you.

spots.name: Original Oyster House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This is a "must do" if you like seafood and historical places. Go back in time while eating the best fish sandwich you'd ever want to eat. Wash it down with creamy buttermilk or a beer. Of course, there are oysters, lightly breaded, or their specialty oysters which are sort of like a fritter. Other seafood dishes and foods are available and all delicious.

spots.name: Aiello's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: In contention for the best pizza in the Burgh, along with Mineo's next door. It's a local favorite, and is a common hang out for many nearby high school students. The pepperoni rolls are to die for, loaded with parm. It has a classic Italian pizzeria atmosphere with friendly and personable staff. They are open till 2AM so you can always grab a cut to go.

spots.name: Jack's Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Open every hour that they are legally allowed to serve alcohol, closing only from 2AM-7AM each morning. A dive bar in the truest sense, and typically the final stop for many on a Carson Street pub crawl. The drinks are extremely cheap. If you are looking for a beer and a shot, this is the bar to go.

spots.name: Delanie's Coffee
spots.summary: Delanie's serves a variety of coffees, teas, and other hot beverages alongside bagels, other lighter fare, and some alcoholic beverages. Drinks can be enjoyed at seating outside, in the loft, and in the main seating area which is open-air when the weather allows.

spots.name: Luke Wholey's Wild Alaskan Grill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Features fresh seafood. $2 oysters. 'Wild' themed art. Young chef with fishing guide experience prepares traditional items with adventurous twist, e.g. grilled swordfish on bed of cabbage, bacon, and roasted potatoes. Grills out front in 'fair' weather.

spots.name: Sree's Foods

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Simple, no-frills Indian restaurant with great food. Their selection isn't big (they usually have only about five dishes per day) and it's pretty low-key (all dishes are served in styrofoam take-out containers), but it's very tasty and inexpensive.

spots.name: 61c Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Named for the bus of the same name that stops nearby. Pretty good coffee, friendly baristas - one of the hipper spots to hang out, usually full of grad students. Free Wi-Fi. There are only 2 outlets for laptops, and they are in high demand.

spots.name: Angelo's Pizza

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Well-known pizzeria owned and operated by a first-generation Italian family. Caters to many hospitals and businesses in the area. Hefty portions, hoagies, hand-crafted pizzas with fresh toppings, and one of a kind homemade “mayonnaise”.

spots.name: Hofbräuhaus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Modeled after the original Hofbräuhaus in Munich, with German style brats and booze. The accordion player (and sometimes other entertainers) keeps the mood festive and energetic, especially once visitors have had a few rounds of beer.

spots.name: Milky Way

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: This vegetarian restaurant has an assortment of pizzas. They have many salads and make a great falafel. The best part about it is that it is kosher. For any people who keep religious eating habits, this would be the place to go.

spots.name: Wiener World

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A small hot dog stand tucked on Smithfield St. There are no tables or chairs here, just one small counter inside and an order window facing the street. But the franks are excellent, as are the fries and fish sandwiches.

spots.name: Fat Head's

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A giant beer selection, truly focusing on local and regional beers, many of them on tap. Giant sandwiches and home cut fries and chips. They have an even larger section in their carry-out store on the 2nd floor.

spots.name: Carson City Saloon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Voted as one of the best sports bars in the city. If you are interested in cheering for a Pittsburgh team, this is the bar to go. If it is the playoffs, show up ahead of time or there may be a line at the door.

spots.name: St Clair Social Pittsburgh Restaurant and Bar

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: For a place that calls itself a "Beer Emporium", it certainly does not disappoint, with more than 20 Belgians on tap among its offerings. A cozy neighborhood establishment, with a pinball machine to boot.

spots.name: Mediterranean Grill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A nondescript entry hides a hole-in-the-wall restaurant below the street level. The menu is predominately Lebanese, but contains a variety of foods in a range of prices. BYOB.
